pr_body:
The rx timeout timer callback need update **trx_state** variable and this variable is protected by a **mutex**. Because of that, when compiling the system with **CONFIG_ASSERT=y** the system reports _ASSERTION FAIL [!arch_is_in_isr()] @ ZEPHYR_BASE/kernel/include/ksched.h:262_.

This refactor the driver remove **trx_state** variable dependency and consequently removes **phy_mutex** and **rx timeout timer** to be compliant with kernel rules.

Fixes: #23198

This PR includes #22511

issue_context.title: rf2xx driver uses mutex in ISR
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

The ieee802154_rf2xx driver is using a mutex in ISR context:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/drivers/ieee802154/ieee802154_rf2xx.c#L85-L87

With CONFIG_ASSERT=y, the kernel will  report

```
ASSERTION FAIL [!arch_is_in_isr()] @ ZEPHYR_BASE/kernel/include/ksched.h:262
``` 

The MCR driver handles this differently, I think.

FYI: @nandojve
comments: @nandojve will you send a fix for this?
@nandojve you can use a spinlock or `irq_lock()/unlock()` instead of a mutex. Or you can schedule the work in the workqueue thread instead with `k_delayed_work()` instead of `k_timer_start()`.
@tbursztyka input welcome for this issue, in case you have a suggestion.
